GitHub Actions’ YAML parser has been quietly accepting documents that violate the official specification, according to a recent investigation.

The core finding is that the parser, built on YamlDotNet 5.3.0, allows a step containing a single‑quoted flow‑style string to pass even though YAML 1.2.2 § 8.2.3 requires an extra indentation level. The offending snippet places the opening quote at the same column as the parent key, which the spec marks as invalid.

What else changed is that the bug persists across versions. Upgrading the library to the current 18.1.0 release does not resolve the issue because the guard for single‑quoted nodes (`!isSingleQuoted`) was never corrected. A 2020 patch only addressed double‑quoted strings, leaving the single‑quoted case untouched.

“GitHub Actions will happily run a workflow that violates the YAML 1.2 specification,” the author notes, highlighting the practical impact on CI pipelines.

Why it matters: tools that enforce strict YAML compliance—linters, static‑analysis plugins, or custom generators—can reject workflows that GitHub runs without complaint, leading to hidden formatting errors and extra debugging effort.

A caveat is that the problem stems from the choice of parser; other hidden incompatibilities may exist until the library aligns with the spec.

How are you handling YAML validation in your CI pipelines given this discrepancy?
